name: Skagit River (Marblemount – Rockport)
blurb: Wide, gentle glacial river — famous for winter bald-eagle floats and an easy summer paddle.

sections.notes: Easy riffles and gravel bars. Watch for wood. No fee: NPS says there is no fee to raft the Skagit in a personal raft (Copper Creek), and USFS says no fees are required at Marblemount Boat Launch. USFS asks boaters to avoid beaching between Marblemount and Rockport bridges.

putInAccess.operator: National Park Service (Ross Lake National Recreation Area, North Cascades NP Service Complex)
putInAccess.sourceName: NPS Public POIs, 'Copper Creek Raft Take-out/Launch' (OBJECTID 20467, type Boat Launch, Ross Lake NRA)
putInAccess.note: Batch 3. Coordinate is NPS's own POI for the raft take-out, 27 m from the v1/AW candidate. Esri World Imagery (z19, checked 2026-10-25, research/raw/batch3/copper.png) puts it on the north bank under trees about 9 m from the water's edge. NPS lists its XY accuracy as 'Unknown'. Legal access: the NPS rafting page (https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/rafting-in-the-north-cascades.htm) says the Skagit is accessible 'via ... the Copper Creek Take-Out near mile post 112' on SR 20; NPS says there is no fee to raft the Skagit in a personal raft.
putInAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
putInAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~271, west), the take-out is on the north bank, right of the NHD centreline (~60 m; ftype 558 artificial path through the wide channel). Confirmed on imagery.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: USDA Forest Service, Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF: Marblemount Boat Launch
takeOutAccess.note: USFS point is the parking loop ~90 m from the Skagit; shoreline under canopy, no ramp visible (research/raw/batch4/mm19_g.png). Restrictions: eagle-season (Dec-Feb): Skagit Bald Eagle area guidance - limited launch hours and no beaching; check before winter trips
takeOutAccess.directions: USFS Marblemount Boat Launch by the Cascade River Rd bridge at Marblemount; the launch is on the right just after the bridge (USFS description), reached from the gravel parking loop.

sections.notes: Classic eagle float. In winter eagle season paddlers are asked to launch between 11 am and noon so eagles can feed undisturbed in the morning. A 2026 AW trip report described heavy new wood between Marblemount and Rockport with ~3 portages — scout and check recent reports. The Cascade River joins just below the put-in, so flow here is higher than the gauge reads. Howard Miller Steelhead Park (Skagit County) charges a small ramp-use fee (AW; amount not verified).

putInAccess.directions: USFS Marblemount Boat Launch by the Cascade River Rd bridge at Marblemount; the launch is on the right just after the bridge (USFS description), reached from the gravel parking loop.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Skagit County Parks and Recreation — Howard Miller Steelhead Park
takeOutAccess.note: The current county directory confirms river access. County Topographic Atlas 2011 page 49 labels Howard Miller Boat Launch here, and the county’s September 2011 kiosk notice independently names this launch. The existing research candidate projects to UTM 10N 603813 E, 5371106 N, matching the atlas launch vicinity; imagery shows the river-side lot west of SR 530. Trees obscure the precise ramp end. Retain Area precision and do not claim a current fee from the old proposed fee schedule.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use Howard Miller Steelhead Park, 52804 Rockport Park Road, Rockport. Follow park signs to the river launch west of the SR 530 bridge. Check current launch fees and posted conditions with the county; the Area marker does not identify the exact waterline.

mapAuditNote: Audited 2026-10-25 (final run). Copper Creek is verified (NPS POI 20467). Marblemount (USFS coordinate is the parking loop) and Howard Miller (Skagit County, no public coordinate) are still pending.
